observations: A large head-like form fills the center, built from overlapping rectangular and rounded shapes in red, blue, pink, and cyan against a flat orange background.
Two asymmetric eye-like openings sit mid-face—the left filled with dark crosshatching under pink, the right outlined in cyan and blue with a rounded spiral center.
Loose purple, yellow, and magenta loops orbit the head, extending past its edges into the orange field, creating a tangled halo of looping lines.
reading: The head reads as a mask or container: rigid rectangular scaffolding in red and blue holds soft pink fills and dark voids. Zigzag lines across the forehead and teeth-like marks along the lower opening give the form a grinning, almost mechanical quality. The orbiting purple and yellow loops feel restless, as though the figure vibrates against its own outline. Here color blocks and line compete for the same space, producing a sense of pressure inside the frame.
contextAngle: In the owned subset, Scrimshaw 18 sits between "Scrimshaw15" and "Scrimshaw 21" by title number. Its flat orange ground and blocky internal geometry contrast with the looser, more linear approach visible in both neighbors, marking a heavier use of color fills within this part of the numbered family.

connections.reason: Both use a saturated yellow-orange ground and exposed teeth-like marks, but Scrimshaw 21 relies on thick black outlines while Scrimshaw 18 buries its outlines under layered color loops.
Both pack a head-like form with dense multicolor lines, yet nnxyz nifty faces #9 builds volume through fine scratches while Scrimshaw 18 uses fewer, bolder strokes and flat color blocks.

lookingQuestion: Where do the loose purple and yellow loops connect to the rigid rectangular shapes inside the head, and where do they break free entirely?
ambiguities: Whether the dark crosshatched areas inside the eye openings are a distinct layer or part of the same drawing pass cannot be confirmed from the image alone.
The relationship between title number order and actual making sequence is unknown; neighbors may not have been created consecutively.
